rationale: We cannot currently tell whether any of the platform's judgement agents are any good, because nothing links a judgement to what happened to it. The auditors (content-quality-auditor 7,119 LLM calls, visual-design-auditor 4,032, site-review-agent 3,987) raise site_work_items via write_audit_findings_action, and those items reach real terminal outcomes (4,599 complete, 200 unresolved, 96 failed, 50 wont_fix, 275 needs_human_review). But the created row records no pointer back to the run that raised it, so the join 'this finding -> this outcome' does not exist. Practical consequence today: an auditor that flags twenty non-issues and one real defect is indistinguishable, in the data, from one that flags twenty real defects — we have no per-agent precision signal, so nobody can tell which auditor is worth its spend or which item_types it over-fires on. This change adds that pointer. Secondary motivation, stated plainly so reviewers can weigh it: the reasoning-dataset workstream needs (reasoning -> outcome) pairs as training/eval labels, and this single field is what makes ~15,000 existing judgement calls per month joinable to ground truth. We are NOT proposing to propagate work_item_id into llm_call_log for these agents — that was our first idea and it was wrong: these agents are item PRODUCERS, not handlers, so no work_item_id exists at their spawn time (verified: none appears as a handler_agent anywhere, and only build-dispatch-loop injects that field). The correct direction is the reverse one, from the created item back to its origin run.

plan.summary: site_work_items records no link back to the orchestration run whose reasoning created it, so agent judgements can never be scored against item outcomes. Add a nullable origin_correlation_id column (plus a partial index), populate it at the two INSERT paths that create items from agent findings (write_audit_findings_action and the discovery_checks registry), and thread it through the WorkItemSpec struct. Nullable and additive: existing rows and all readers are unaffected.

edits.rationale: A first-class join key belongs in a column, not smuggled into the spec JSONB. spec holds the defect's domain data and is read by handlers and verifiers; adding provenance to it would overload a field whose consumers do not expect it. site_work_items already carries provenance-shaped columns (source, created_by, batch_id), so this follows the established shape. Nullable with no backfill: historical rows genuinely have no known origin and should read as unknown rather than be guessed at.

This is the path by which every auditor finding becomes a work item, and it is where the originating run is in scope. params.ExecutionContext carries the correlation id, so no new plumbing is needed to obtain it. Adding one column to an existing INSERT keeps the change inside the statement that already writes batch_id and created_by.

The second path that creates items. Its doc comment already notes it mirrors a parallel workItem struct in run_discovery_checks_action.go; adding the field in one and not the other would widen an existing divergence, so both move together (next edit).
edits.sketch:
type WorkItemSpec struct {
     SiteID       uuid.UUID
     PageID       *uuid.UUID
     ...
     ItemKey      string
     BatchID      uuid.UUID
+    // OriginCorrelationID is the orchestration run whose findings produced
+    // this item. Zero value means unknown and is written as SQL NULL.
+    OriginCorrelationID *uuid.UUID
 }

edits.rationale: Keeps the two parallel item-creation shapes in lockstep. If only the audit path carried provenance, a reader could not tell 'no originating run' from 'this path forgot to record it' — which is exactly the ambiguity this change exists to remove, so a half-applied version is worse than none.
edits.sketch:
Mirror the WorkItemSpec field onto the local workItem struct and add
origin_correlation_id to this file's INSERT column list and VALUES, sourced
from params.ExecutionContext.CorrelationID with the same nil-safe parse as
the write_audit_findings_action edit. No behaviour change when absent.

plan.risks: site_work_items is a hot table; an ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN of a nullable column with no default is metadata-only on modern Postgres and should not rewrite the table, but a reviewer should confirm the server version and that no long transaction is holding a conflicting lock at apply time. The new partial index adds a small write cost on insert. Deliberately NOT touched: the idx_swi_dedup unique index and workItemTerminalStatuses in work_items_common.go — this change adds no status and alters no dedup key, so the index/Go-list lockstep contract (which has caused fleet-wide 42P10 before) is untouched; a reviewer should nonetheless confirm the dedup index does not need to include the new column (it should not — provenance must never affect dedup identity, or the same defect from two runs would stop deduplicating). Migration numbering must follow the ledger discipline in bugs_open/007 (migrations ledger omission trap). Backfill is deliberately out of scope: historical rows have no recoverable origin, and inventing one would poison the very join this creates.
